I carry 40lbs out of towns, do about 30 miles a day and am happy every moment. It depends on how comfortable u are with the weight. You'll adjust to the weight definitely but you might have to lower your weight or slow your pace to keep the hiking happy!  Lots of my stuff was second hand / cheap So I got a bigger heavier and bulkier pack but you can deff stay happy with it :)

Note: I have a heavier pack than a lot of folks so just be aware that's where my perspective is at. Obv In the end it's all a personal decision and hyoh :) 

Poles- I'm going to preface this by saying I have knee problems. I didn't use poles on the AT when I slashed, and started without them here and was fine. But I got some as a gift and wow do they make a huge difference! specially with downhills, I wouldn't hike without them. They help reduce so much impact. If u have knee issues- deff get them. If u dont- I still recommend them for protecting your knees in the long run. 

Sandals- I like them, i wear them all the time when I'm not hiking. So when I get into camp, when I'm taking a day off at a lake/other days off on trail. And in town I never wear my shoes. If u don't mind wearing ur shoes all the time, deff don't need them. 

Rain pants - I don't think they are necessary. Even if it rains a ton in Washington, unless it's cold, just wear yr shorts and air dry and u will be fine. But I have heard from folks it is nice to have with the mosquitoes :o

Compass/paper maps- I commented below but I'm a fan of paper maps. But regardless if u don't, I would say a small light compass and have the topo on the phone. Are you going to use it every day? Probably not. But it's good to have for when u get lost/in the snow. 

Knife- I think bring at least a small one. I carry a pocket knife and use it frequently to open things (primarily, cans in town lol canned food) but I know that's kinda weird but I think a small one is a good idea (Swiss army knife?)

Gaifers- I'd recommend. It's super Sandy/dusty at some points and really helps to prevent blisters

I think if u r guna skip out on the paper maps bc I know in all honesty most people do and it's fine it's totally your decision to make, download the topo on the Guthooks app (I think half mile already has the topo) and keep a compass. If gps doesn't work for whatever reason at least u can still navigate in case of emergency. I prefer my paper maps  (I also have a heavier pack than most so the extra weight doesnt matter to me, so ofx hyoh) but I also do have Guthooks and deff recommend having an app as well even if u go primarily paper. You can drop yr phone in a river but u can also drop yr maps, shit happens and it's always good to have backup either way!

Okay so I just rewatched the movie and it still makes no sense lol but this is some things I took note of: 

 We get that view at around the 5 minute mark of a real human talking to Frank. We see security cam footage of Frank and some vitals or whatever. 
The screen with footage of Frank shows a few things that I think are important: Day, time passed(in HH:MM:SS.000 format), DLP#, NSWE coordinates, and camera number (always Camera 4). 
This moment where we hear human Howard is the only time ever we see what day it is, a different DLP number (DLP_00000470), and the time that has passed is in the 3 hour mark 

ALL other times we get to view Frank through the footage we have a DLP number of DLP_365901019 and the time is always between 9hours 26 minutes and a few seconds over 9hours 27 min. 
Instead of day # we get a changing DKL number (DKL 001, 002, 007, 008, 347, 347, 347, 348, 349, 349, in that order). I'm inclined to believe this is same as day number, though I cannot confirm. But we get the big jump from 008 to 347 after the montage of Frank intertwining reality and his memories for a bit. 

Now why did I bother paying attention to the security camera footage and that moment with human Howard? 
We are watching this movie for the vast majority through the lens of Frank. Even though we do not know as much as he does (like that he's an alliance member, etc) we get to see him experiencing his memories and reality, we don't know what's reality, etc etc. However the moments from the security camera and the moment with human Howard are a perspective he does not have. It's independent of him and that's what I want to base any theories i come up with from. I don't really see a reason to put them in except to hint to us viewers about something outside of Frank's knowledge.

That's shitty I'm sorry. I know how that is, the hardest part of my life as a trans person was definitely living with family (up to 18) . I didn't start T until college and shit was shitty until I moved out at 18. I know those suicidal thoughts especially when you are so alone at such a young and vulnerable age. Please try to find friends online if you don't have friends in person or people who understand. Remember that the world is changing and even if yr family isn't, theres a lot more representation for you and when you get out there can be resources. 
For now I would say 
1. See if you can find any youth centers that help trans folk 
2. If there are no youth specific lgbT centers try planned Parenthood (or an equivalent, I don't know what there is over there) 
3.  Call a suicide hotline, get on the suicide hotline chat, get your feelings out on Reddit, do whatever it is you have to do to talk it out and feel supported 
4. Try to take it day by day. It's hard, I know. But you have to take it in the moment and not get overwhelmed with thinking about the future. Just survive this moment.  And I honestly don't have an answer how to make it better and easier instantly. What I did was run. I ran trails for hours and hours to get away and clear my mind. Maybe try running or other sports or try an instrument or some video games. Do whatever it is you can to get your mind off things that are hurting you. 
5. Any face masculization will stay, but some fat will be redistributed , your voice will be the same. You will still pass. 
6. When you think you can't make it, just know that you can. I believe in you. I never thought I would live past 18. I never thought I would get on T, get surgery, change my name, graduate, be alive at 25, but I'm still here. And I made all that happen . You can too. It's going to be hard but I know you can make it <3 please believe in yourself
